title: French Validation of the SAHOT Outcome Scale After Subarachnoid Haemorrhage
official: Validation of the French Version of the Subarachnoid Haemorrhage Outcome Tool (SAHOT): a Prospective Single-Centre Cohort Study
summary: Survivors of subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH) frequently experience cognitive, psychological, physical and social sequelae, but no French-language instrument covers all these dimensions. The SAHOT (Subarachnoid Haemorrhage Outcome Tool), developed and validated in English, is a SAH-specific patient-reported outcome measure. This prospective single-centre cohort study aims to validate the French translation of the SAHOT in adult patients seen at a follow-up consultation within 12 months after a SAH of any aetiology. The primary objective is to assess the internal consistency of the French SAHOT. Seventy patients will be included; accompanying relatives may also be included to complete a proxy version of the questionnaire.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria (patients):

* Age over 18 years
* Subarachnoid haemorrhage of any aetiology
* Onset less than 12 months before inclusion
* Seen in consultation at the Hôpital Fondation Adolphe de Rothschild
* Judged able to complete a self-administered questionnaire by the evaluating clinician
* Informed and not opposed to participation (or relative's non-opposition if the patient is under guardianship and/or unable to consent)

Inclusion Criteria (relatives):

* Age over 18 years
* Relative / caregiver of a patient with subarachnoid haemorrhage within the previous 12 months
* Attending the follow-up consultation of an included patient
* Informed and not opposed to participation

Exclusion Criteria (patients and relatives):

* Non-French-speaking
* Psychiatric disorder judged incompatible with completion of the questionnaires by the investigator
